A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same T1 study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendix A contains relocated setup material and additional response transcripts.

before.justification: v1 reports original T1 benchmark accuracies, sampling and penalty ablations, inference-scaling experiments, and reasoning-behavior analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally provides full model-response examples in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The CoT initialization, oversampling, high-temperature sampling, leave-one-out normalization, entropy bonus, KL normalization, EMA reference update and response penalties are unchanged. The truncation-and-summarization procedure is also retained.

E1.justification: Both use MATH-train and NuminaMath for training and MATH500, AIME2024, Omni-MATH-500 and GPQA for evaluation. The added MATH500 example comes from existing coverage and introduces no new task or scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical comparator membership, including GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-sonnet, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, o1-preview, QwQ-32B-preview and the GLM/Qwen/SFT models. No additional comparator appears in the appendix.

E3.justification: v1 Section 4.1 moves to v2 Appendix A.1 with unchanged data construction, training settings, model sizes, generation limits, greedy decoding and Pass@1 evaluation. The inference-truncation evaluation protocol is likewise retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A expands the existing AIME case into a full transcript and adds a MATH500 worked example illustrating reasoning behavior. Existing sampling, temperature, penalty, inference-scaling and key-step analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report averaging 32 AIME evaluations and retain the same shaded training plots. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or explanations of the shading.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports a MATH500 response ending in 1736 and expands the already reported AIME example ending in 721. Tables 1–3 and the matched plots retain their numerical values and trends; no aggregate performance gain is newly reported.

T1.justification: The RL objective, reward and KL normalization, entropy term and EMA equations are unchanged apart from numbering and typesetting. The appended mathematical calculations are model-response examples, not new theoretical results about T1.

C1.justification: The central claims about exploration-driven RL, stronger reasoning performance and inference scaling without additional verification remain. Details shortened out of the abstract, including the QwQ comparison, remain elsewhere in the paper.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning exploration, reflection, generalization and training collapse are retained. The new impact statement is generic; it adds no substantive limitation, applicability boundary or revised interpretation of results.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future release of model weights and SFT/RL training data; v2's introduction states that they are publicly available at the same repository. This changes reported resource availability, while the training and evaluation details are principally relocated unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bai et al. (2022) on RLHF and cites it alongside Ouyang et al. in Related Work. The remaining cited works and the paper's positioning around reasoning, RL scaling and inference scaling are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, and experimental setup moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix A.1. The abstract and introduction are condensed, the title gains T1, and impact, acknowledgment and full-transcript material are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Figure 5 is rearranged vertically, v1 Figures 8–9 are merged into v2 Figure 8, and the original response example moves to Appendix Figure 9 alongside new multipage transcript boxes.

improvement.justification: The full transcripts make the qualitative evidence more inspectable, and v2 reports model and training-data availability rather than a planned release. These provide limited transparency and reproducibility gains. The method, quantitative evidence and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, and the additional example supplies illustration rather than systematic validation.
